title: Load test burst behavior + validate neighbor impact stays within SLO guardrails
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Run production-representative load tests that exercise Dedicated “burst capacity” behavior and validate we do not regress non-burst tenant latency/throughput SLOs.

Why this matters
- Burst is explicitly allowed to improve bursting tenant throughput during peaks, but MUST NOT create noisy-neighbor impact on other Dedicated tenants sharing the region/hardware class.
- We need evidence for GA gates and a repeatable harness for future tuning (fairness weights, cooldowns, pool sizing, circuit breakers).

Scope
- Multi-tenant burst pool scenarios (single region/hardware class per run; start with us-east/H100).
- Admission controller + routing integration path (real policy decisions, denial reason codes, fallback/backpressure behavior).
- Neighbor impact measurements (tail latency deltas and tail amplification), plus platform safety signals.

Non-goals
- Full end-to-end cost/margin validation (covered by metering + Finance reconciliation).
- Cross-region bursting tests (out of scope for initial release).

Test environment
- Staging “perf” cluster with dedicated burst pool resources (mirrors GA topology as closely as possible).
- Use redwood-loadgen + scenario runner added in PR-23890.
- Configure 3–5 synthetic tenants with deterministic traffic profiles and pinned model/version.

Key scenarios
S0: Baseline / no burst
- 3 tenants, each at baseline reservation, steady QPS, 60 min run.
- Purpose: establish baseline p50/p95/p99, error rates, and admission controller overhead.

S1: Single-tenant burst spike
- Tenant A bursts from baseline -> +2.0x (or configured max burst ratio) for 15 minutes.
- Tenants B/C remain steady at baseline.
- Validate: A throughput increases; B/C p95 latency delta stays within guardrails; denials are explained and consistent.

S2: Competing bursts (fairness)
- Tenants A and B both request burst concurrently (different priorities/tiers if supported in environment).
- Validate: fairness enforcement prevents starvation; distribution matches configured weights; denial reasons make sense (pool_saturated vs tenant_cap vs cooldown).

S3: Burst cap reached / customer-visible behavior
- Tenant A hits configured per-tenant burst cap.
- Validate: routing behavior follows spec (429/backpressure or queued behavior depending on endpoint policy); retry guidance is correct; no runaway queue depth.

S4: Telemetry lag injection
- Introduce controlled telemetry staleness (or simulate by pausing fleet telemetry updates to admission controller for N seconds).
- Validate: determinism + smoothing prevents “flapping” denials; no pathological oscillations; guardrails continue to protect neighbors.

S5: Circuit breaker / fleet safety cap
- Drive pool to high saturation and cross fleet safety thresholds.
- Validate: global circuit breaker triggers correctly; burst is reduced/disabled; non-burst latencies recover; alert annotations are emitted.

Measurements (must capture per-tenant + aggregated)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end (gateway -> response) + model execution time where available.
- Tail amplification: (p99 - p50) and p95 delta for non-burst tenants vs baseline.
- Errors: 429/overload responses, timeouts, admission errors; breakdown by denial reason code.
- Admission controller overhead: request/decision latency, error rate, timeouts.
- Pool health: saturation %, queue depth, telemetry lag, circuit breaker state.

Success criteria (GA gate inputs)
- Non-burst tenants (B/C) during S1/S2:
  - p95 latency regression <= 5% vs baseline for sustained 10-min windows.
  - p99 latency regression <= 10% vs baseline (investigate any >10% spikes; must be attributable and correctable).
  - Error rate does not exceed baseline by >0.05% absolute (excluding intentionally induced overload/429 scenarios).
- Bursting tenant (A):
  - Throughput increase observable (>= 1.5x effective tokens/sec vs baseline during burst window) unless limited by tenant cap.
- Determinism:
  - Given identical configs and load profile, denial reason distribution should be stable run-to-run (within expected noise).
- Safety mechanisms:
  - Fleet safety cap / circuit breaker triggers when expected and recovers within 5 minutes after load reduction.

Deliverables
- Load test harness changes + scenario configs checked in (see PR-23890) with docs for running locally and in CI.
- A single “results” summary pasted into this ticket: run IDs, dashboards links, and pass/fail against criteria.
- Any discovered issues filed as follow-up ENG tickets with clear repro.

Owners / reviewers
- Owner: Peter Holtz (Routing SRE)
- Review: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead), Mina Haddad (Routing), Keiko Yamamoto (Guardrails)

Notes
- Prefer testing with production-like prompt/token distributions (long-context + short chat mix) rather than constant token sizes.
- Keep label cardinality under control in any new metrics emitted by the harness (align with observability taxonomy).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run S0–S5 scenarios in staging-perf with repeatable configs and produces a run report (tenant-level latency, error rates, denials, saturation).
Non-burst neighbor impact remains within defined thresholds for S1/S2 under expected peak loads.
Denial reason codes are present and stable (no large unexplained 'unknown' category).
Circuit breaker behavior is verified (trigger + recovery) and annotated in dashboards/alerts.
Any violations are converted into actionable follow-up issues with owners and proposed mitigations.
activity: 2025-04-08 (Talia Benson): Created ticket as GA gate requirement. Please treat as P0; leadership asked for evidence that non-burst tenants are protected before expanding beta.

2025-04-10 (Peter Holtz): Aligned with Mina/Elena on using routing integration path (no bypass). Will base scenarios on load-test harness from PR-23890 and pull denial breakdown from new metrics in PR-23822.
2025-04-15 (Allison Grant): Reminder: keep per-tenant labels bounded (tenant_id hashed or mapped to 3–5 synthetic tenants). Avoid raw request_id in metrics. Use run_id only in logs.
2025-04-18 (Peter Holtz): Implemented scenario runner config for S0–S3 locally; staging-perf wiring pending admission controller rollout in us-east/H100.

2025-04-23 (Keiko Yamamoto): Requested S4 telemetry lag case. Beta hotfix PR-23944 suggests smoothing helps; please ensure lag injection reproduces the prior failure mode so we can validate it's fixed.

2025-04-29 (Peter Holtz): Ran S0/S1 initial in staging-perf (run_id: perf-2025-04-29-01). Observed neighbor p95 delta ~+2–3% during A burst window; p99 had two brief spikes (+14%) correlated with admission controller timeouts. Filed follow-up to tighten admission timeout + fallback path.

2025-04-30 (Peter Holtz): Follow-up filed: 'Admission controller timeout causes routing retries and p99 spikes in staging-perf' (linked in related_issues once created). Temporary mitigation: lower admission RPC timeout and avoid retry-on-timeout for burst-only path.

2025-05-06 (Peter Holtz): Re-ran S1 after timeout tuning (run_id: perf-2025-05-06-02). Neighbor impact improved: B/C p95 delta <= +1.8%, p99 delta <= +7% sustained; errors unchanged. Bursting tenant throughput +1.6x. Looks within gate.

2025-05-09 (Peter Holtz): Ran S2 fairness case with two concurrent burst tenants (run_id: perf-2025-05-09-01). No starvation observed; allocation followed weights within ~5%. Denial reasons primarily pool_saturated and tenant_cap as expected.

2025-05-13 (Peter Holtz): Ran S4 telemetry lag injection (run_id: perf-2025-05-13-01). Confirmed previous 'flapping' denials no longer present; denial rate stable, neighbor p95 delta <= +3%. This appears to validate PR-23944 smoothing/guard conditions.

2025-05-17 (Peter Holtz): Ran S5 safety cap / circuit breaker (run_id: perf-2025-05-17-02). Circuit breaker triggered at configured saturation threshold; burst admissions dropped to near-zero within ~30s; non-burst latencies recovered within 3–4 minutes after load reduced. Alerts fired with correct annotations (no paging in staging).

2025-05-20 (Sean Gallagher): Reviewed results vs criteria. Looks acceptable for GA gate for us-east/H100, assuming we keep SLO regression auto-gate enabled (PR-23988) and retain ability to kill-switch per region.
2025-05-22 (Peter Holtz): Marking Done. Results summary + dashboard links stored in internal run log (ref in links). Any remaining improvements tracked separately; main gate criteria satisfied.
